item.title: Eagles' sudden about-face on IR for Jalen Hurts seems odd, to say the least
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Saturday morning arrived with an ESPN report from its top two insiders regarding the Eagles having no intent to place quarterback Jalen Hurts on IR.
item.content:encoded:
Saturday morning arrived with an ESPN report from its top two insiders regarding the Eagles having no intent to place quarterback Jalen Hurts on IR. Per the article from Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport (who in recent months have morphed from Batman and the Joker into Batman and Robin), the Eagles have "not even discussed the possibility of injured reserve."

Then came 4:00 p.m. ET and the deadline for locking the roster for Week 6. Hurts was placed on injured reserve.

It's unclear what happened between Saturday morning and Saturday afternoon. One more-than-plausible explanation is that the Eagles and Hurts received more medical information, and a possibility that supposedly wasn't even on the radar screen suddenly became the obviously correct destination. The Saturday morning report, however, points to a possible disconnect within the organization as to how the Hurts situation should be handled.

Beyond the odd notion that the Eagles hadn't even considered the possibility of placing a player taking blood thinners to resolve a blood clot on IR, the original article carried hints that the Eagles and Hurts weren't on the same page.

"The ultimate decision about when Hurts returns to play will come from his medical team, and the Eagles are ready to follow his lead," the Saturday morning ESPN report explained. The article also suggested that "some around the team might consider Hurts week-to-week," hours before Hurts was shelved for at least four weeks.

Perhaps the team was still tiptoeing around acknowledging the severity of the situation, given that it allowed him to play last Sunday in London with a blood clot in his leg — and in light of the barest of bare bones disclosure to the public about Hurts's true health condition. Indeed, it's fair to wonder whether the Eagles (and the league) allowed Hurts to play with a blood clot in order to avoid the P.R. mess that would have unfolded if a player who had fully participated in practice all week, who had no injury designation for the game, and who was never downgraded to questionable once the clot was discovered was suddenly scratched from the active roster.

Regardless, the Saturday morning report from ESPN conflicts so sharply with the Saturday afternoon roster move that it invites outsiders to conclude that the team wants everyone to know that the decision to not play Hurts was made by Hurts and his doctors and not by the team.

Either way, Hurts is out for at least the next four games. And possibly longer. The full extent of the absence depends on how long it takes for the clot to be cleared by blood thinners, and whether the situation further deteriorates.

The overriding point is that Hurts has a potentially serious health condition. He was nevertheless permitted to play an entire game with it one week ago. More recently, the team (per the ESPN report) hadn't even entertained the idea of giving him four games to heal.

Whether intended or not, the reporting and the ensuing about-face will make some think the Eagles and Hurts had different ideas on how to best proceed.

item.title: C.J. Gardner-Johnson suspended for one game
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Bills have their bye in Week 7, but when they come back, they will not have one of their key defenders.
item.content:encoded:
The Bills have their bye in Week 7, but when they come back, they will not have one of their key defenders.

The NFL announced on Monday that safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson has been suspended one game for spitting at an opponent during Sunday’s win over the Raiders.

Gardner-Johnson was ejected from the contest.

The league notes Gardner-Johnson was suspended for unsportsmanlike conduct, with his actions violating Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which applies to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.”

Gardner-Johnson is in his first season with the Bills. He has registered 26 total tackles with two passes defensed and one interception so far this season.

Bills head coach Joe Brady called Gardner-Johnson’s actions “uncalled for” in his postgame press conference.

“It can’t happen,” Brady said. “It’s going to be addressed. The team is way more important.”

Buffalo will host Baltimore in Week 8. While Gardner-Johnson may appeal his suspension, he’s currently eligible to return for the Bills’ Week 9 road matchup against the Vikings on Monday Night Football.

item.title: Giants release Jihad Ward
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Linebacker Jihad Ward's second stint with the Giants has come to a quick end.
item.content:encoded:
Linebacker Jihad Ward's second stint with the Giants has come to a quick end.

According to multiple reports, the Giants have released Ward on Tuesday morning. Ward was signed off of the Vikings' practice squad in late September.

Ward played 41 defensive snaps and four special teams snaps in his two appearances with the team. He was credited with one tackle.

Ward also played in 34 games for the Giants during the 2022 and 2023 seasons. He moved on to the Vikings in 2024 and played for the Titans in 2025 before returning to Minnesota at the start of this season.

item.title: Alec Pierce not ready to return to practice this week
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: While Colts receiver Alec Pierce is eligible to return to the field this week, he still needs more time before he's ready to practice.
item.content:encoded:
While Colts receiver Alec Pierce is eligible to return to the field this week, he still needs more time before he's ready to practice.

Head coach Shane Steichen said in his Monday news conference that Pierce, who is on injured reserve, will not practice this week as he’s still in the rehab process.

Pierce aggravated the heel injury he had surgically repaired in the offseason during Indianapolis’ Week 2 loss to Kansas City.

The NFL’s leader in yards per reception in each of the past two seasons, Pierce had five catches for 72 yards before he was sidelined.

item.title: Stefon Diggs: It's still wide open for us
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Commanders fell to 1-4-1 when the clock ran out on Monday night, but wide receiver Stefon Diggs chose to accentuate the positive in the locker room after the game.
item.content:encoded:
The Commanders fell to 1-4-1 when the clock ran out on Monday night, but wide receiver Stefon Diggs chose to accentuate the positive in the locker room after the game.

Diggs's third quarter touchdown catch was part of a 14-point run that pared down a 20-point 49ers lead and gave the Commanders a chance to move ahead late in the fourth quarter. A long drive ended on fourth down in the red zone and the 49ers moved to 6-0 with a 23-17 lead, but Diggs said that the effort the Commanders showed and the fact that the 49ers are an outlier when it comes to their record are reasons to hold onto hope heading into their bye week.

"It’s still wide open," Diggs said, via Marshall Kramsky of WUSA. "Where we are and where the league is, it’s kinda interesting. A weird spot right now. Nobody’s kinda made it clear — that team we just played is a helluva football team. That’s one of those guys that’s gonna be in the running. . . . We played a decent game, we could’ve played a lot better. We were still in it, just like all these games we’ve been in the past couple weeks. We’ve been in it, we just gotta find a way to pull ‘em out."

Diggs isn't wrong about things being open in the NFC East. No team in the division has won a game since Week 4 and two of the other three teams in the division have lost their starting quarterbacks for the season, so the prospect of someone running away with things feels remote. That said, the Commanders have consistently fallen short in the biggest moments of games and that provides little reason to think they're going to suddenly go on a run of their own.

The door is open for Diggs and company to prove otherwise, however, and that's about all you can ask for after winning once in six weeks.

item.title: Dan Quinn on viral clip: "I definitely knew it was fourth down"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The first half of Monday night's game included a failed fourth-and-two play by the Commanders from the San Francisco 13.
item.content:encoded:
The first half of Monday night's game included a failed fourth-and-two play by the Commanders from the San Francisco 13. After the pass to the end zone landed incomplete and the Commanders were called for an illegal shift, ESPN's cameras caught Commanders coach Dan Quinn seemingly surprised to learn it was fourth down.

When he met with reporters nearly an hour after the game ended, Quinn was ready for the question regarding the viral lip-reading moment.

"I definitely knew it was fourth down," Quinn said. "We were going for it, and I was — I think what you're referring to, I was probably saying, like, with the illegal shift, there's not a penalty to go for a field goal. Like, it doesn't go, like, it's the turn on downs. Like, I think somebody asked me, 'Can we kick a field goal?'  So, now we were going for it. We knew we had to go for some fourth downs to be bold in the game. I didn't think it was gonna be a 17-14 game.  I probably thought it was gonna need 28, 30 to score, you know, to go win it. And so it was by design that we were gonna go, but I knew what happened. I think, I probably was just commenting that I remember, at least on the headset, somebody asked me, after an illegal shift, like it was turnover on downs, and [quarterback] Jayden [Daniels] saw the foul, too.  He also came out and saw the penalty."

You can watch the clip and come to your own conclusion. Again, he seemed to be surprised, not stating a fact. And he clearly had his story ready when he arrived for his press conference — along with plenty of time after the game to craft it.

Obviously, after what happened last week, Quinn couldn't afford to admit he didn't know it was fourth down. Even if he didn't know it was fourth down.

item.title: Kyle Shanahan: Eddy Pineiro has got to make his extra points
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: 49ers kicker Eddy Pineiro missed another extra point on Monday night.
item.content:encoded:
49ers kicker Eddy Pineiro missed another extra point on Monday night. Coach Kyle Shanahan was not happy about it.

Pineiro has been one of the worst kickers in the NFL this season, missing three extra points and three field goals, and Shanahan said after Monday night's win over the Commanders that it can't go on this way.

"Yeah, he's got to make them," Shanahan said. "He missed another one today. Fortunately it didn't get us, but I think everyone knows the answer to that, you've got to make your extra points."

Pineiro has a long history of not making his extra points: Over the last five seasons, he has missed 14 extra point attempts, the most of any kicker in the NFL, and among the 30 kickers who have attempted at least 75 extra points over the last five years, Pineiro has the lowest percentage of made kicks. If Pineiro keeps missing his job may not be safe.

item.title: Jed York's suspension ends today
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: York returns after a six-game ban and $500,000 fine.
item.content:encoded:
The 49ers have played their sixth game of the season. That means owner Jed York has served his full suspension.

As the league explained when announcing the ban earlier this month, York may return on October 20.

York self-suspended for three games, and he got credit for those games when the league added three more. He also was fined $500,000.

Whether that means he'll return to games immediately remains to be seen. The 49ers face the Falcons in Atlanta on Sunday before entering the annual bye.

The quarterly ownership meeting is set for New York on Tuesday and Wednesday. He's now free to attend, if he chooses.

There's still a basic and fundamental disconnect between owner and player suspensions when it comes to the financial realities of the punishment. Players, when suspended, lose all of their compensation and potentially have to repay money already received. Owners pay a fine that pales in comparison to the money they make.

Case in point: York lost $500,000 for his six-game suspension. For a one-game suspension due to sucker punching Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb, Rams tackle Alaric Jackson lost $934,555. And Bears defensive end Montez Sweat loses $2.18 million for his two-game suspension under the PED policy.

While the violations aren't apples-to-apples (York's suspension arose from an effort to harvest an apple from a poisonous tree at a trailer park), the numbers are the numbers.

One game for Jackson equals $934,555. Two games for Sweat equals $2.18 million. Six games for York equals $500,000.

It's an obvious issue that few discuss. Which means there's no chance of the approach ever changing.

item.title: U2 to perform at halftime on Thanksgiving Eve
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: U2 performed a memorable halftime show in New Orleans at Super Bowl XXXVI in 2002 and they will be back on a football field for a brief concert later this year.
item.content:encoded:
U2 performed a memorable halftime show in New Orleans at Super Bowl XXXVI in 2002 and they will be back on a football field for a brief concert later this year.

Netflix announced on Tuesday that the band will perform at halftime of the NFL's first ever Thanksgiving Eve game on November 25. The game will be at SoFi Stadium with the Rams hosting the Packers.

“There's a reason U2 has headlined stadiums for decades: they don't just perform, they deliver iconic moments audiences remember forever," Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos said in a statement. "We’re thrilled that they'll bring that same magic to the NFL stage on Netflix. It’s going to be an unforgettable night for football fans and Netflix members worldwide.”

Netflix has carried Christmas games the last two seasons and halftime shows for those contests have featured artists like Beyonce and Snoop Dogg, so they may have more to announce ahead of the two games they'll be broadcasting on the holiday this year.

item.title: Shane Steichen on Chris Ballard's firing: "I don't think it falls completely on Chris"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: In January, Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon put both coach Shane Steichen and G.M.
item.content:encoded:
In January, Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon put both coach Shane Steichen and G.M. Chris Ballard on clear notice. On Monday, she fired Ballard.

Steichen, who possibly remains in place only because there's no viable interim replacement on his staff (and because the Jeff Saturday experiment has already been attempted), addressed the dismissal of Ballard with reporters on Monday.

“It’s the shitty part of the business," Steichen said, via Stephen Holder of ESPN. "I don’t think it falls completely on Chris. I’m the head football coach. It takes all of us. Coaches, scouts, everybody.”

He's right, and Irsay-Gordon could be firing everybody, in time. For now, Ballard was the easiest person to replace in response to a devastating home loss to the previously winless Titans.

Barring a turnaround from 2-4 to a playoff appearance, Ballard will soon have company in the category of former employees of the team. And while the absence of a clear choice to serve as interim coach may have saved Steichen for now, it's hardly a guarantee that he'll be in the job when the season ends.

item.title: PFT's Week 7 2026 NFL power rankings
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Niners stay on top.
item.content:encoded:
1. 49ers (last week No. 1; 6-0): Kyle Shanahan is having his best year yet.

2. Chiefs (No. 2; 5-0): Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III is the NFL MVP so far.

3. Bills (No. 4; 5-1): The defense still needs plenty of work.

4. Jaguars (No. 3; 4-2): They're finally getting a return on the Travis Hunter investment.

5. Vikings (No. 6; 5-0): Some tough games are coming.

6. Broncos (No. 7; 4-2): They'll go as far as the offense can take them.

7. Seahawks (No. 5; 3-3): They should've kept Kenneth Walker III.

8. Patriots (No. 9; 4-2): The injuries are piling up before a short-week trip to Chicago.

9. Packers (No. 11; 4-2): They're getting Josh Jacobs back at a perfect time.

10. Bears (No. 15; 4-2): A franchise quarterback makes all the difference.

11. Browns (No. 12 (tie); 4-2): Szmyt happens, in the bad way before the good way.

12. Ravens (No. 8; 4-2): They need Lamar Jackson back in the lineup.

13. Steelers (No. 12 (tie); 4-2): Time to get Le Torchon Terrible ready.

14. Bengals (No. 12 (tie); 3-2): They need to start stacking some wins.

15. Panthers (No. 18; 3-2): Two years after being benched, Bryce Young is earning a big contract.

16. Raiders (No. 16; 3-3): Can the most popular team in L.A. send the Rams into a deeper hole?

17. Rams (No. 10; 2-4): The 13th overall pick should've been used on a receiver.

18. Lions (No. 21; 3-2): The next two games (Packers, Vikings) could shape the season.

19. Texans (No. 24; 2-4): They're in the same position they were in a year ago, but with a better record in the division.

20. Saints (No. 25; 2-4): The Gayle Benson bounce is real.

21. Giants (No. 17; 3-2-1): J.J. McCarthy time is coming.

22. Cardinals (No. 29; 2-4): Maybe they should move to L.A.

23. Cowboys (No. 20; 2-4): Cheap does as cheap is.

24. Falcons (No. 22; 2-4): They should change their name to the Vampires.

25. Eagles (No. 19; 2-4): The questions about the handling of Jalen Hurts won't be going away, no matter how badly they want them to.

26. Titans (No. 31; 1-5): Can they build on their unlikely win in Indy?

27. Colts (No. 23; 2-4): Is a fire sale coming?

28. Jets (No. 26; 2-4): With the Dolphins coming to town, Sunday becomes a must-win game.

29. Buccaneers (No. 27; 1-5): If they'd known what Jalon Daniels can do, would they have extended Baker Mayfield?

30. Commanders (No. 28; 1-4-1): Dan Quinn's time is up. And the end result likely won't be a tie.

31. Dolphins (No. 32; 0-5): "Thank you, Mike McDaniel."

32. Chargers (No. 30; 0-6): Has any team ever failed so badly to live up to their preseason expectations?

item.title: John Harbaugh on RB timeshare: Someone has to "do something" to earn job
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Giants running backs ran 14 times for 34 yards in last Sunday's loss to the Saints and one of their backs said after the game that he thinks the rotation of backs is working against the team.
item.content:encoded:
Giants running backs ran 14 times for 34 yards in last Sunday's loss to the Saints and one of their backs said after the game that he thinks the rotation of backs is working against the team.

Najee Harris and Devin Singletary had four carries in the game, Tyrone Tracy had six and Cam Skattebo didn't touch the ball at all after leading the team in carries through the first five weeks of the season. Harris said, via Greg Johnson of the Trentonian, that it is "hard to get into a rhythm" while constantly going in and out of the game and those comments were brought up to head coach John Harbaugh during Monday's press conference.

Harbaugh said he understands that feeling, but said that the opportunity to develop that kind of rhythm is something that has to be earned and no one has done that to this point.

"I would love for us to be in that kind of a circumstance," Harbaugh said, via a transcript from the team. "A Derrick Henry circumstance or a Saquon Barkley circumstance or whatever it might be. That would be great, and we haven't. Our run game hasn't earned that yet, and none of those guys have. My advice would be to any player, and it's all the guys, we had the same conversation. I've had the same conversation with all the running backs, the receivers, it's no different than any position, but do the most you can with the opportunities you get. Make the most of those opportunities and you're sure to get more opportunities. Do something."

The Giants made the choice to move on from Barkley before Harbaugh was in the organization, but invoking Henry is interesting because he and the Ravens were criticized in Week 16 last season for pulling Henry in favor of Keaton Mitchell at key moments in the second half against the Patriots. New England came back from 11 points down in the fourth quarter for a 28-24 win that helped keep the Ravens out of the playoffs and contributed to Harbaugh being fired at the end of the season.

No one would argue that any of the Giants backs are in Henry's class, but history says that the division of labor might not be any more ideal if that was the case.

item.title: Cardinals' two wins are the two biggest upsets in the NFL this season
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Cardinals are only 2-4, but their two wins have been big ones.
item.content:encoded:
The Cardinals are only 2-4, but their two wins have been big ones.

Specifically, they've been the two biggest upsets in the NFL this season: When the Cardinals beat the Rams on Sunday, they were 12.5-point underdogs. That was the biggest upset of the year, surpassing the Cardinals' Week 1 win over the Chargers, when they were 9.5-point underdogs.

There have only been seven games this season when the point spread was more than nine points. Those two games that the Cardinals won as underdogs, and five other games in which the underdogs lost by a combined 72 points.

Both of the Cardinals' wins this season have been at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles, where they have two wins, the Rams have one and the Chargers have none. Don't bet against the Cardinals, at least not in Los Angeles.

item.title: Brock Purdy is the NFL's all-time record holder for highest career passer rating
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The NFL has a new all-time record holder for highest career passer rating: Brock Purdy.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL has a new all-time record holder for highest career passer rating: Brock Purdy.

As of Monday night, Purdy has the highest passer rating in NFL history, at 105.6. To qualify for the official career record, a player needs to have thrown at least 1,500 passes in his NFL career, and on Monday night Purdy topped the 1,500-attempt mark, giving him the passer rating record.

In all, Purdy has completed 1,038 of 1,524 passes for 13,145 yards, with 98 touchdowns and 39 interceptions.

The record previously belonged to Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson, who has a career passer rating of 102.7. He's followed by Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers at 101.8, Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow at 101.3 and Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes at 100.8. Purdy will probably keep the record for a while, as he's far enough ahead of the pack that no one would surpass him unless he has a disastrous end to the season while one of those quarterbacks behind him puts up record-setting numbers. There are also no other quarterbacks who are close to 1,500 pass attempts whose passer rating could surpass Purdy.

Passer rating is determined by a complex formula that combines completion percentage, yards per pass, touchdown percentage and interception percentage. The NFL adopted it as the league's official statistic for ranking passers in 1973. It's far from a perfect method of ranking quarterbacks — it ignores first downs, sacks, fumbles, rushing and other measurements of a player's quality — but as a rough gauge of how well a quarterback is playing, it's not bad. And it ranks Purdy ahead of every quarterback, ever.

item.title: Terry McLaurin believed to have season-ending knee injury
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin had to be carted off the field with an air cast on his left knee on Monday night and the image didn't do much to conjure up hopes of a quick return to the field this season.
item.content:encoded:
Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin had to be carted off the field with an air cast on his left knee on Monday night and the image didn't do much to conjure up hopes of a quick return to the field this season.

Head coach Dan Quinn confirmed that the team feared a "significant" injury after the game and that McLaurin would go for tests on Tuesday to determine just how significant it is. Those tests are pending, but Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that the team is bracing to learn that McLaurin will miss the rest of the season.

McLaurin missed Week 4 with a hamstring injury and has 15 catches for 230 yards and a touchdown on the season.

McLaurin has two more years left on his contract and is set to have a $34 million cap number in 2027, but there's no guaranteed money left on the deal should the Commanders opt to move in a different direction.

item.title: Aaron Glenn: Frank Reich is doing a good job as offensive coordinator
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Jets finished 29th in points scored during Aaron Glenn's first season as their head coach, so it was not a great surprise that they made the choice to fire offensive coordinator Tanner Engstrand at the end of the campaign.
item.content:encoded:
The Jets finished 29th in points scored during Aaron Glenn's first season as their head coach, so it was not a great surprise that they made the choice to fire offensive coordinator Tanner Engstrand at the end of the campaign.

Frank Reich was the choice to replace him and the Jets acquired quarterback Geno Smith while making other changes to the unit, but the results have not been much different through six games. They are 27th in points scored, dead last in red zone efficiency and in the bottom portion of the league in a number of other metrics. It hasn't helped

Their Week 6 loss to the Patriots turned in part on a pair of failed fourth down conversions that saw the Jets get stopped short on a pair of runs, which is also something that contributed to their loss to the Packers in Week 2. On Monday, Glenn was asked if he's happy with what he's seen from Reich thus far.

"I think he's done a good job. I really do," Glenn said, via a transcript from the team. "Obviously, there are a number of things that we can improve on, and I think I just told you guys that from short yards to two-minute, but that also goes on me also when it comes to the defensive side, me and [defensive coordinator Brian] Duker on some things that we have to get better at, too. We have to improve on some things and that's what the season is. That's what practice is. After six games, it's hard to just say, 'Okay we're this.' We have to see how this thing plays out, but I would say I think he's done a good job. . . . As we continue to go through this season, I'll continue to see us progress and getter better on the things we have to get better at. To answer your question, I think he's done a good job."

Injuries have kept running back Breece Hall and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell off the field in recent games while first-round pick Omar Cooper just got back on the field after a Week 1 ankle injury. Cooper had a strong game against the Patriots, which was a promising development for what Reich could do with a full hand but more tangible results will have to come one way or another for the Jets to improve on a 2-4 start.

item.title: Joe Brady says Bills won't be cutting C.J. Gardner-Johnson after spitting incident
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The two players involved in spitting incidents during games were (and still are) star players.
item.content:encoded:
The two players involved in spitting incidents during games were (and still are) star players. After Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter was ejected before the first play from scrimmage in Week 1 (which was later treated as a suspension) and Bengals receiver Ja'Marr Chase was suspended after completing a game in which the spit was missed, there was zero talk about the players being cut.

With safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson doing it on Sunday in Las Vegas, the question was asked on Monday whether the Bills will cut him after he missed half of a game after an ejection and all of the next game due to a suspension.

"Look, C.J.'s a member of the Buffalo Bills," coach Joe Brady told reporters. "We brought him here for a reason, and we know that he knows that he has to play better. He knows he has to be better for this team, and, you know, just like everybody else, right, we've got to learn from this stuff, and we have to improve and find ways to get better as the season goes."

Brady then started to compare Gardner-Johnson's spitting to running back James Cook's fumbling problem. Brady seemed to edit himself in real time.

"No different than — it's different, right? — Jimbo fumbling," Brady said. "You know, we have to continue to find ways to get better, and he knows that he has to be better, and, you know, it's just an opportunity for him. Look, it'll be an opportunity for someone else to, you know, play early the week and step up, but it is an opportunity for him to grow and be better as a better teammate and a better football player, you know, when this opportunity comes up again."

Like Brady said, the Bills brought Gardner-Johnson to town "for a reason." They wanted his edge and attitude. That comes with the full package of who he is. Sometimes, Gardner-Johnson will cross the line. (And, sometimes, a teammate may get a taste of it.)

It's part of the total package. Brady made it clear on Monday that the Bills are willing to tolerate the less savory aspects in the name of getting the dynamic they want on their defense.

item.title: Sean McVay on Kyren Williams: "He was emotional after the game"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: After Sunday's loss to the previously 1-4 Cardinals, Rams running back Kyren Williams had a simple explanation for the team's inconsistency on offense.
item.content:encoded:
After Sunday's loss to the previously 1-4 Cardinals, Rams running back Kyren Williams had a simple explanation for the team's inconsistency on offense.

"Probably because I’m not out there," Williams said in the locker room.

On Monday, coach Sean McVay was asked whether he has spoken to Williams about his remarks.

“I have," McVay told reporters. "He brought it up to me. I wasn't aware of it. He's such an energy for us. He was emotional after the game. I know this guy's heart. He wants to make sure that he's influencing and effecting positive change. I think what he said it was more of, ‘I just always want to try to be that spark.’

"He was frustrated after the game, but his teammates know what he's about. When he explained it to me, I totally understood where he was coming from. He's a great leader for us. I think the way that it was interpreted was not what his intentions were. I know his teammates and I felt that way. He actually brought that up to me on his own. I was not aware of it until he brought it up to me.”

Against the Cardinals, Williams was on the field for 42 snaps, or 72 percent of the total workload. Blake Corum had 16 snaps, or 28 percent.

Williams had 10 carries for 50 yards, and Corum had nine for 42. (Williams had three catches for 17 yards, and Corum had two for 18 and a touchdown.)

Through six games, Williams's usage rate is at 71 percent, with 110 touches for 610 yards. Corum stands at 27 percent, with 56 touches for 314 yards.

The concern, then, doesn't seem to be just playing time. Corum gets the ball more frequently when he plays — 47.45 percent of the time. Williams gets the ball 35.94 percent of the time he's on the field.

Either way, Williams said what he said. And, as McVay explained it, Williams raised it with McVay and explained himself.

item.content:encoded:
Although an unresolved question lingers regarding whether or not the numbers are inflated by anyone who visits Amazon Prime and gets an autoplay video of the game, the official, Nielsen-generated numbers for Prime Video's Thursday Night Football keep improving.

The Week 6 game between the Seahawks and Broncos averaged 16.26 million viewers. In its fifth game of 2026, Prime Video posted a higher number than the corresponding week in 2025.

The five-week average is 17.29 million, a nine-percent bump over the 2025 pace, and 13 percent above the full-season average.

The 2026 Week 6 audience bested the 2025 Week 6 audience (Eagles-Giants) by one percent.

This week, the schedule deals Prime Video a good one — the 4-2 Patriots vs. the 4-2 Bears. Hopefully, neither of the quarterbacks will play like "garbage."

item.title: Kyle Shanahan: Mike Evans injury is not a long-term thing, hopeful he can play Sunday
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans had to leave Monday night's game because he aggravated the Achilles injury he has been dealing with, but coach Kyle Shanahan said after the game that they're optimistic Evans will play on Sunday against the Falcons.
item.content:encoded:
49ers wide receiver Mike Evans had to leave Monday night's game because he aggravated the Achilles injury he has been dealing with, but coach Kyle Shanahan said after the game that they're optimistic Evans will play on Sunday against the Falcons.

Shanahan said Evans is used to dealing with this injury and just needs to manage it.

"It's something that he's had before," Shanahan said. "It's something that bothered him throughout the week. So when you have Achilles tendonitis like he does, it kind of is what it is. Flared up tonight, I hope he recovers throughout the week, but you don't think it's a long-term thing. It almost cost him this game and ended up costing him two quarters and hopefully he'll be able to play next week. But if not, we'll have to have the rest of the group step up and hopefully get him healed up by after the bye week."

The 49ers were beating the Commanders 20-3 when Evans went down, and it looked when Evans left the game like they'd win a blowout. But the Commanders came back and could have taken the lead in the fourth quarter before the 49ers ultimately escaped with a 23-17 win. Shanahan said Evans' absence hurt in the second half, although he also said there were a lot more factors that made the game close.

"It's definitely a big deal when you lose a player like Mike," Shanahan said.

Shanahan is optimistic he won't have to play without Evans again on Sunday.

item.title: NFL has until Tuesday to decide whether to flex Eagles-Commanders out of prime time
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: With the Eagles slipping to 2-4 and the Commanders sliding to 1-4-1, the two teams have a Week 8 prime-time date looming.
item.content:encoded:
With the Eagles slipping to 2-4 and the Commanders sliding to 1-4-1, the two teams have a Week 8 prime-time date looming. And if the league is considering a flex (as it reportedly was out of last week), the clock is ticking.

By rule, Tuesday, October 20, is the deadline for moving the Sunday night game.

The problem is the absence of clear options. Ravens-Bills makes the most sense, but the Ravens play the following Thursday night. Vikings-Lions is a possibility, if the NFL is willing to commit now to flexing Lions-Vikings in Week 15 out of Sunday night.

Colts-Jaguars wouldn't have as much sizzle as Eagles-Commanders, given the wide-open nature of the NFC East. The Jaguars are off this week, so they're guaranteed to enter the game at 4-2. The Colts, who face the Vikings on Sunday and who have fired their G.M., could be 2-5 by Week 8.

Browns-Steelers and Chiefs-Broncos are presumably off the table because the first game between the rivals was televised in prime time. (By rule, at least one game of a home-and-home division rivalry must be televised on Sunday afternoon.)

It's ultimately the league's decision. By tomorrow night, everyone should know what it is.

item.title: What's next for Dan Quinn?
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: At the end of the first half of Monday night's game, with the Commanders down 20-3 and coach Dan Quinn going viral based on a lip-reading clip that was being widely interpreted as him not realizing it was fourth down (after a failed fourth-down play), it looked like Quinn was on track to get fired after the game.
item.content:encoded:
At the end of the first half of Monday night's game, with the Commanders down 20-3 and coach Dan Quinn going viral based on a lip-reading clip that was being widely interpreted as him not realizing it was fourth down (after a failed fourth-down play), it looked like Quinn was on track to get fired after the game.

Then came the second half, and an effort by the Commanders that made the final score (23-17) far more respectable.

So now owner Josh Harris has a decision to make. One week removed from the humiliating clock debacle and entering the bye week, will Harris make a change?

Even with the six-point margin, the Commanders remain 1-4-1. Working in Quinn's favor is the fact that the division is still there to be had, if they can turn it around.

The other consideration is that the bump from making an interim hire could also give the team the kind of wakeup call that could carry them to an NFC East title. (At that point, however, it would be difficult to not reward the interim coach by giving him the permanent job.)

There's a mini-bye looming, between the Week 10 Thursday night game against the Giants and the Week 11 Monday night game against the Bengals. Maybe Harris will decide to kick the can, giving the Commanders three more games (Eagles, Rams, at Giants) before making a final decision.

item.title: Monday Night Football: 49ers hang on for 23-17 win over Commanders
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Commanders had two drives deep into San Francisco territory to win it in the final two minutes.
item.content:encoded:
The Commanders dug a hole in the first half, and the 49ers were throwing dirt on top of them in the third quarter.

San Francisco led 20-3 at halftime and 23-3 with 18 seconds left in the third quarter. It came down to the last play.

The 49ers held on for a 23-17 victory that was too close for comfort for the home fans. The 49ers are 6-0, and the Commanders are 1-4-1.

The Commanders had 17 plays, two first downs and 90 yards in the first half. The 49ers had 41 plays, 17 first downs and 303 yards in the first half.

The second half was all Washington, with Jayden Daniels throwing two touchdown passes and giving the Commanders a chance to win.

The Commanders outgained the 49ers 224 to 72 in the second half.

On Washington's next-to-last possession, the 49ers had the Commanders stopped on Romello Height's sack of Daniels with 2:55 left. But Ashtyn Davis was called for illegal contact. It was one of four defensive penalties the 49ers had resulted in Commanders' first downs.

The Commanders faced a fourth down at the San Francisco 17, and Daniels gave Treylon Burks a chance to catch a touchdown pass. Burks had it briefly before Malik Mustapha forced it out as Burks hit the ground in the end zone with 1:54 remaining.

The 49ers' last three drives were three-and-outs, gaining a total of 7 yards. That gave Washington a second chance for a miracle comeback.

49ers gunner Siran Neal was called for fair catch interference on the punt, and the 15-yard penalty gave Washington the ball at their own 46. The Commanders reached the San Francisco 28 before Daniels was called for grounding, and on the final snap, Ogbo Okoronkwo and Height combined for a sack of Daniels. It was one of four sacks for the 49ers.

Brock Purdy was 21-of-29 for 264 yards and a touchdown. He lost his star wide receiver, Mike Evans, before the end of the first half. Evans aggravated his Achilles soreness and missed the second half after making three catches for 94 yards in the first half.

Christian McCaffrey rushed for 64 yards and two touchdowns on 16 carries and caught nine passes for 53 yards. George Kittle made five catches for 69 yards and a touchdown.

Daniels was 29-of-40 for 300 yards and two touchdowns. He lost his star wide receiver, Terry McLaurin, to a knee injury in the first quarter, and nine different Commanders receivers caught at least one pass.

item.title: Stephen Jones: Brian Schottenheimer "absolutely" has full support of ownership
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Cowboys have slumped to 2-4.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys have slumped to 2-4. Does second-year head coach Brian Schottenheimer still have the full support of ownership?

"Absolutely," Stephen Jones said Monday when asked that question on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, via Todd Archer of ESPN. "There's not any question in Jerry's and I's mind. He has the team. There's no question they want to go out there and execute and make things happen. We feel really good . . . about our coaching staff. We just have to continue to evolve and get to a point where we can win these football games."

True or not, it's the only answer Jones could give in a public setting. They still need the fans to believe in the coaching staff; if ownership doesn't, why should the fans?

And even though the Cowboys have fallen flat in three straight prime-time games, they have a very winnable game against the Eagles next Monday night. Primarily because the Eagles are currently in as much disarray as any team in the league, if not more.

Besides, the division is there to be had. The Giants have lost their starting quarterback for the year, the Eagles have lost their starting quarterback for the year, and the Commanders are currently too inconsistent. If Dallas can get its act together, the Cowboys could win the division and host a playoff game.

Conversely, failure to turn it around could raise plenty of questions. Schottenheimer could be out. And if/when there's a new coach, who knows how different the roster might look?

For now, yes, they'll fully support everyone. If they fail to win what is becoming a none-of-the-above division, that could change. Quickly.

And, ar that point, the only person who would be safe is the G.M.

item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans has three catches for 94 yards, but his night might be over.
item.content:encoded:
49ers wide receiver Mike Evans has three catches for 94 yards, but his night might be over.

Evans entered the game with Achilles soreness, and he aggravated the injury late in the first half. The 49ers list him as questionable for the second half.

His return seems unlikely given the 49ers are in full control, up 20-3 at halftime.

Evans stayed on the ground after going low to catch a 16-yard pass from Brock Purdy with 1:10 remaining in the first half. Evans walked directly to the training room for treatment, and he has not returned to the sideline for the start of the second half.

Evans entered the game with 24 catches for 326 yards and three touchdowns.

UPDATE 10:04 P.M. ET: The 49ers have ruled out Evans.

item.title: Monday Night Football: 49ers lead 20-3 at halftime, but Mike Evans leaves early
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The 49ers star wide receiver appeared to aggravate his sore Achilles late in the first half.
item.content:encoded:
The 49ers were far from perfect in the first half.

The Commanders had drives to the San Francisco 33 and 13; kicker Eddy Piñeiro missed his third extra point of the season; running back Christian McCaffrey lost his first fumble since Week 12 of 2024; safety Malik Mustapha had his second helmet-to-helmet hit of the season, though he wasn't penalized; and tight end Luke Farrell had two penalties for 25 yards.

The 49ers, though, were good enough, taking a 20-3 lead into the locker room at halftime.

San Francisco gained 303 yards, with Brock Purdy going 17-of-22 for 214 yards and a touchdown. Mike Evans caught three passes for 94 yards. McCaffrey had 16 touches for 82 yards and two touchdowns. Kittle had four catches for 34 yards and a touchdown.

Evans has been battling Achilles soreness and appeared to aggravate the injury on a 16-yard catch with 1:10 remaining in the first half. He walked directly to the training room for treatment after the play.

The Commanders had two first downs, 17 plays and 90 yards. Jayden Daniels was 7-of-10 for 88 yards, and for the second consecutive week, he made a poor decision. Daniels threw away a fourth-and-2 pass with the Commanders on the San Francisco 13.

The Commanders lost star wide receiver Terry McLaurin with a knee injury. He was carted off the field in the first quarter and almost immediately ruled out. Wide receiver Stefon Diggs appeared to injure a finger on Mustapha's illegal hit, but he returned to the game. Defensive tackle Javon Kinlaw limped off the field after McCaffrey's touchdown run with 13 seconds left in the half.

item.title: Commanders WR Terry McLaurin carted with knee injury
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The team has ruled out McLaurin, who was injured in the first quarter.
item.content:encoded:
Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin was carted off the field with a left knee injury.

49ers cornerback Deommodore Lenoir was tightly covering McLaurin on a third-down play with 2:16 remaining in the first half when McLaurin's left leg gave out. He went to the ground, grabbing at his left knee and appeared to be in significant pain.

The team's medical staff placed a vacuum splint on McLaurin's leg before helping him onto the cart.

Players from both teams wished him well before he left.

The Commanders' other star wide receiver, Stefon Diggs, took an illegal hit from safety Malik Mustapha that wasn't penalized. Diggs' right hand hit Mustapha's helmet, and he appeared to injure his ring finger.

Diggs has returned to the game after getting treatment.

item.title: Jim Harbaugh on Mike McDaniel: "We're looking into everything"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel remains employed, for now.
item.content:encoded:
Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel remains employed, for now.

The key words may be "for now."

Coach Jim Harbaugh was asked about McDaniel's status on Monday. Harbaugh did not declare McDaniel to be safe.

"We're looking into everything at this point, and that process is ongoing," Harbaugh said. "Particularly offensively, scoring more points. . . . 0-6 does not give the privilege to rule out anything at this point, and we're looking into everything."

There's a belief in some circles that McDaniel will be relieved of his duties, and that he'll be replaced by pass game specialist Adam Gase, the former head coach of the Jets and Dolphins.

McDaniel was hired by the Chargers after Harbaugh fired Greg Roman. From 2022 through 2025, McDaniel served as head coach of the Dolphins.

The Chargers are off in Week 7, so they have a little time to make a decision. It's possible, as one source put it on Monday, that the team is considering whether to reassign McDaniel and, if so, what his new role would be.

Regardless, until Harbaugh declares McDaniel will continue in his current job, there's a real chance he won't.
